findings.title: [intake] How many controller cycles does one CAS occupy the data bus for in the abstract PHY model, and must the scheduler space CAS commands by it? data_path_mapping implies host_width_bits / ddr_channel_width_bits beats at one beat per controller cycle (2 here), while timing_model.tCCD (4 nCK = 1 controller cycle) lets the scheduler issue a CAS every cycle: two reads one cycle apart cannot both be captured on one bus.
findings.detail: phy_interface.data_bus_cycles_per_cas is not stated. With the spec silent, the data path and the DRAM model both assume one beat per controller cycle and the scheduler assumes JEDEC tCCD; back-to-back CAS then overrun the data bus, whatever the data path does (drops before 65dbb0f, shifted/zero words after it). Either the scheduler enforces tCCD_eff = max(tCCD, beats) or the beat model moves to the real rate (a word per nCK, BEATS_PER_CYC = 2 x clock_ratio); until decided the scheduler spacing is the safe reading. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: Frontend HANDOFF_VALIDATION_2026-10-29 (BEATS_PER_CYC question) and Validation's hybrid judgement of 65dbb0f: data_path stage 0/19 on path_03, conservation clean (2026-10-29).

findings.title: [intake] When the data path's write buffer is full, does the host port stall writes (wr_data_ready reaches wb_stall_o), or is the buffer sized so that it can never be full while the queue has room (write_buffer_depth >= command_queue_depth + writes in flight)?
findings.detail: host_interface.write_buffer_backpressure is not stated. Today write_buffer_depth = command_queue_depth = 16 and wr_data_ready has no consumer: a write word is dropped whenever the buffer is full in the cycle the queue accepts another write (1 of 600 on the refresh paths, drop e5ec723f495e, 2026-10-29). Either answer closes it; the first needs a new edge in the Phase 1/4 manifests. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: CONSERVE/WRITE_REQUEST_TO_DATA on path_05/path_20, drop e5ec723f495e (2026-10-29).

findings.title: [intake] Must the host port return acknowledges in the order the beats were accepted (Wishbone B4 pipelined masters match acks to requests by order; a response carries no id), or may a write be acknowledged ahead of an earlier read that is still waiting for its data?
findings.detail: host_interface.ack_ordering is not stated. The design acknowledges a write one cycle after acceptance and a read when its data returns, tens of cycles later, so a write accepted after a read is acknowledged first. A B4 master counting acks attributes that ack to the read and takes whatever is on wb_dat_o as its data. Validation's monitors and driver attribute read responses by rsp_valid, not by ack order, so this is not caught today; if the answer is in_request_order it becomes a check and a finding, if writes_may_complete_early the host contract must say so. Disposition: decision — comparisons that depend on this are UNDETERMINED until the spec states it. First encountered as: review of the HOST_001 fix (write acks now queued behind read acks, 1fe4c9d, 2026-10-29).
